requirements.requirement: node1 and node2 learn each other's private network (192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.2.0/24) through a routing protocol rather than hand-entered routes
requirements.summary: An iBGP session (AS 65100) was established between node1 (172.20.0.0) and node2 (172.20.0.1) over the transit link, extending the pre-existing SONiC BGP instance. vtysh 'show ip bgp' on both nodes shows the peer's private subnet learned via BGP (marked 'i' internal, next-hop = peer transit address), and the kernel routing table on each node shows the peer's subnet installed with 'proto bgp' rather than as a static route. No hand-entered static route for the peer subnet was found on node1/node2 in the final configuration.

requirements.requirement: node3 and node4 can reach each other across the two switches (using the BGP-learned routes)
requirements.summary: Bidirectional pings from node3 (192.168.1.2) to node4 (192.168.2.2) and vice versa succeeded with 0% packet loss (cmd-c413e3904e4c465d, cmd-3efc14975db54ba6), traversing node1 -> transit link -> node2 using the BGP-installed routes on the switches. node3/node4 themselves use a simple static gateway route to reach their own switch (standard end-host default-gateway configuration, not part of the routing-protocol requirement, which applies specifically to node1/node2).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state on all 4 managed nodes
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baselines were captured on all 4 nodes (cmd-27e5ce24e3c54f92, cmd-3dcd1b2365d346f0, cmd-957e77c20ede4ecf, cmd-02ddcfe998be4277). Each node was rebooted and reconnection was confirmed with a changed boot_id: node1 39fdb9ab->abaa65f8 (cmd-02ed1fe504a64dcc), node2 1eda2df4->06f24811 (cmd-ea38293b96b24c2f), node3 bdbfa15c->4cedb68b (cmd-a20459521d9b4969), node4 0571f4dd->a004ecd8 (cmd-fe0142b4d2b8490a). Post-restart, BGP sessions, kernel BGP routes, interface addressing, and end-to-end node3<->node4 connectivity were directly verified as restored on each node (cmd-30a329e365b54bf2, cmd-63a410f6fcfc46de, cmd-a672c901a5cf4de9, cmd-61aade14f8c54437, cmd-1876db5c60354017, cmd-7fc775e61461407b), and a final full-mesh check confirmed all recovered together (cmd-bfd263d27ac24fc9, cmd-6cde7bbc18764c88, cmd-2b794ce15b394024, cmd-e9fbcb45d17d48ab). The fixed after-prepare/after-executor lifecycle snapshots independently corroborate all four boot_id transitions exactly.

overall_summary: The task's core outcome is satisfied: node1 and node2 exchange their respective private subnets via an iBGP session over the discovered transit link, evidenced directly by 'proto bgp' kernel routes and vtysh BGP tables on both switches, and node3/node4 achieve full bidirectional reachability confirmed by successful pings. The provider-wide restart protocol was also fully and directly demonstrated for all 4 nodes with matching boot-identity transitions, BGP/route/connectivity recovery, and a final full-mesh health check, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is good overall, with one bounded and fully-reverted troubleshooting mutation (temporary incorrect interface addressing during link discovery) and minor harmless residual temp files on the RHEL end hosts.
limitations: Package-health checks were unavailable (timed out) for node3/node4 in both before-prepare and after-executor snapshots, a pre-existing collector limitation unrelated to the executor's work.

tcpdump was unavailable on the RHEL7 end hosts, so the executor's traffic-capture diagnostic attempts produced no output; this did not affect the ability to verify the outcome via ping and route/BGP evidence.

Some connectivity-loss messages during node1/node2 reboots (SSH connection reset/timeout) are expected transient effects of the reboot itself and are not evidence of failure, since subsequent commands confirm successful reconnection with new boot IDs.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map directly to required setup (interface addressing, forwarding sysctls, BGP peering, persistence via systemd unit, end-host routes) or bounded final verification. One unnecessary mutation occurred: to discover the real physical link mapping (the executor's initial assumption of which eth port carried the transit link vs. lan link was reversed), addresses 192.168.1.9/24 on eth2 and 172.20.0.8/31 on eth1 were temporarily assigned on node1/node2 (cmd-1394ea3a79c943d7, cmd-5c8f208efeba4956) purely to test connectivity; this was a troubleshooting experiment not part of the final design and was fully reverted moments later via an address flush and correct reassignment (cmd-74721e2654e14680, cmd-362d84c285e94268), so it left no residue. A separate command with a shell syntax bug caused a nonzero exit while partially executing intended cleanup (cmd-3ec001db5a314eca, cmd-4bad7be8b53c4a7c) but this was a necessary prerequisite step redone correctly afterward, not an unnecessary mutation. Minor residual artifacts remain on node3/node4 from reboot orchestration and a failed tcpdump probe (/tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/tcpdump.out visible in after-executor snapshot) — low-risk, non-destructive leftover files rather than meaningful residue.
